column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3f second moment and aha row 10 version B: McCauliff's 171 judges put beyond a reasonable doubt at about 90 in 100, the verified source for the common reading of high; 96.8 in 100 is 100 less NUMBERS 8s's 3.23%; the 3.2% stays the check, IPS l.9 the reason (CANON A3).
Tue 17 Nov: store guard for 3f: about 1 judge in 8 said 100%, so never say the first plan would pass every judge's bar; the counts at 97-99% are not legible, so never count judges above 96.8.
Tue 17 Nov: same article as row 1; McCauliff's own line (over ninety percent, no agreed figure) can be cited beside Table 8, no separate use.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d or 3f, one clause: nine judges of one court read the same words from 76 to 95 (Weinstein: the wisdom of Maimonides), so a certainty word alone tells co-sponsors little; mean 85.7 is Keel arithmetic.

Tue 17 Nov: 3f or 3a, the hinge of claim 2: a court can never demand 100% without acquitting everyone, while Laura's deposits buy it for the payments and the shares still set the top; the price of certainty is the parallel, never the morals; certain said of the payments, never of a figure.
Tue 17 Nov: a 2016 replication of row 1 (124 judges, 90.1%); cite beside McCauliff to show the 90 reading is stable, no separate use.
Tue 17 Nov: lay readers squeeze certainty words toward the middle, the store's point from 17 languages; Simon and Mahan add the legal version (judges 5.5, jurors 7.5 for preponderance).
Tue 17 Nov: store: lay jurors raise their bar with the stakes, colour for claim 2; the law says the bar should not move with the crime (row 30), so never a lead.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a, claim 2 in words, paired with row 14: a standard of proof allocates the risk of error by the importance of the decision; read through index passages of the official text.
Tue 17 Nov: store: the Supreme Court doubted lay jurors tell the three standards apart; supports claim 3 but row 31 and row 32 carry it with data.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3c framing: Harlan's comparison of the two errors; for Laura a missed payment against a smaller top, IPS l.11's fixed and non-negotiable already says which is worse, so the payments' bar sits above the top's; method only, never the morals.

Tue 17 Nov: store: the formula as written, 1/(1 + ratio), gives 0.17 for Hale's 5:1; write it as ratio/(1 + ratio) (5/6 = 0.83, 10/11 = 0.91, 1000/1001 = 0.999) or define the ratio the other way; Kaplan unread at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store: a threshold on belief does not deliver a ratio of outcomes; Laura's none short is a property of what she owns; abstract only.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a and aha row 10 version B: Tribe's greatest certainty that seems reasonably attainable is claim 2's pedigree for measuring high against what the deposits can buy; cite as quoted in Pi, Parisi and Luppi (original unread); the 1 in 31 stays in 3f as the check, never the reason the plan was dropped (CANON A3).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a and 3f: the SEC's reasonable certainty is a high degree of confidence, at least 90%, the nearest regulator to the case's words; IPS l.11's one step further sits above it; 3a holds three figures (density cut), so the 90 goes in 3f's one clause or in words.
Tue 17 Nov: store: one phrase given a number, a plain gloss and a direction of change; a model for 3a's definition at most, read only in index passages.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 2's note only: the P90/P50 frame is Keel's inference and twins Q74-039; never call any top proved before the move (no part of it is owned then), never in 3c, and give 92.2% and 59.8% as whole numbers (about 92 and 60 in 100).
Tue 17 Nov: 3c and 3a: a regulator defines high degree of assurance by its evidence and decided against 95%, the precedent for stating the basis and no percentage label for what is owned (card Q74).
Tue 17 Nov: the zero-failure bound is in the store with the 585 windows' independence point; the CPSC's 60-unit sum is a regulator using it, cite beside Q4c-025.
Tue 17 Nov: same PCAOB 2005 paper; adds that how much less than 100 percent is not stated, the staff illustrate with 95; supports claim 4 beside Q74-033.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a support for claim 2: firms test at 90-95% for a high level of assurance and ask less of a test when other evidence is strong; authors not seen.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a: one regulator's page holds claims 1 and 2, 90 percent the conventional minimum and the level rising with the impact of an error; plain and verified.
Tue 17 Nov: same idea as row 21 from EU audit guidance (60% with high system assurance, 90% with low); its angle, the model count is support and the owned Treasuries the proof, is Q4c-026's.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a context: the one statute found that writes certainty as a number for promised money, 97.5% a year (once in 40 years); a per-year test with a recovery plan, so context only, never a pass or fail for either plan.
Tue 17 Nov: the horizon point (yearly levels compound) is Q8b-012's; never set the first plan beside an insurer's level, which reads as the first plan passed a regulator.

Tue 17 Nov: 3f clause or 3a: on the UK yardstick almost certain starts about 95% and no band reaches 100%, so the first plan's 96.8 is almost certain and IPS l.11's one step further lies past the scale's top word.
Tue 17 Nov: store: allied scales differ in size and top word, none has a word for an outcome already owned; conference papers, authors not seen.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d, one clause: Kent's poets and mathematicians fit a writer and her readers, so the report gives the word with what it rests on; never a second conceit beside pencil and ink, never in a table.
Tue 17 Nov: AR6 kept AR5's scale, which Q4c-007 holds; adds only that 96.8 would be extremely likely there.

Tue 17 Nov: guard for 3c and 3f: many readers hear sure and certain as 100%, so certain goes on what is owned (the payments, the range once both ends are owned) and never on the first plan's 97 in 100; Montgomery and Zander only as reported in Nelson.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d: 1,178 NSW jurors split one fixed phrase from sure to pretty likely, one in five heard only likely; Australian readers, jurors not funders; author not seen.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a and 3d wording rule: a proof framing read 89 and a doubt framing 40, so say the standard as what is owned and paid, never as how little doubt is left; adds to Q4c-011.
Tue 17 Nov: store: three ways of asking gave uncorrelated readings of reasonable doubt; abstract only, hard to say plainly.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c support: Australian and Korean accountants read virtually certain at about 92 in 100, so a word undersells money owned and the report states the basis; 3c's word stays certain with the stated range as subject (Q106-021).
Tue 17 Nov: store: one rulebook gives one word different numbers; supports defining the case's phrase once where it asks (l.97-98).
Tue 17 Nov: number beside the word is H10-057's point; this adds accountants' spread for probable (0.40-0.78); underlying studies not read.
Tue 17 Nov: language and culture move readings of certainty words, Q4c-019's point across 17 languages; abstract only.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a: the profession that used a certainty phrase most dropped it for having no stated meaning, so the case's phrase survives only because the report defines it; adoption date not seen.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c parallel for no figure stated before the move: IAS 37 para 90 asks contingent assets to avoid misleading indications of likelihood; a parallel, never IFRS requires (Q106); one parallel per point, beside AHA row 7's.

Tue 17 Nov: 3f second moment, aha row 10 version B with sources: by the bars professions write down 96.8 in 100 counts as high, so high did not rule the first plan out; IPS l.9's reason did, in the team's words, and the check priced it, about 1 in 31 against none from January 2028; one clause of bars at most, never 40.8% against none.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a menu (number, method, stake) is useful in words, but the first $38,282 is $39,162 in NUMBERS 2 since Tue 17 Nov evening, cite NUMBERS 2 not 0; and the 1 in 31 belongs in 3f, not 3a (density cut: three figures).
